campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council is set to consider extending an interim ordinance tied to a state Senate bill, and hold hearings on revoking the business licenses and tobacco permits of two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council will also vote on applying for a regional transportation grant and approving new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of interim ordinance implementing a state Senate bill
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Application for One Bay Area Grant funding for public works
Approval of new consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 6, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council is moving forward with annual approvals for a special assessment district (the Engineer's Report and Resolution of Intention), holding a public hearing on the matter, and setting up a related ordinance for final adoption at the next meeting on May 20, 2026. The council will also discuss whether Saratoga should consider becoming a charter city and review early estimates of possible new local tax options and how much revenue they could generate.
keyTopics: Preliminary approval of the Engineer's Report for the upcoming fiscal year
Resolution of Intention and public hearing on a city assessment district
Scheduling an ordinance for final adoption on May 20, 2026
Exploring whether Saratoga should become a charter city
Reviewing early estimates of potential new local taxes and expected revenue

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — April 21, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council covered routine business including approving prior meeting minutes and reviewing February's financial report, plus authorizing a construction contract and a multi-year professional services agreement. The meeting also included a court-ordered hearing on appeals, meaning the council was required by a judge to formally consider certain appeals brought by residents or parties.
keyTopics: Approval of April 7 closed session meeting minutes
February 2026 monthly financial and investment report
Construction contract awarded to QLM, Inc.
Resolution directing preparation of town improvement plans
Three-year professional services agreement and a second amendment to an existing agreement
Court-ordered hearing on pending appeals

san-jose.title: San José City Council — June 23, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council is considering a mix of items including historic landmark status for a South Sixth Street property, a possible November 2026 ballot measure on ranked choice voting for filling vacant mayor or council seats, a contract for large advertising signage at the airport, and a long-term power purchase agreement with Shell Energy. The meeting also included standard public comment opportunities on agenda items and other city business.
keyTopics: Historic landmark designation and Mills Act tax contract for 647 South Sixth Street
Proposed charter amendment allowing ranked choice voting to fill Mayor or Council vacancies, for the November 2026 ballot
Contract award for large format advertising signs at San José Mineta International Airport
Long-term power purchase agreement with Shell Energy North America
Public comment process and multilingual access options for the meeting

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's City Council met to handle a mix of honors and budget business: they recognized National Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's new judicial appointment, while also closing a private legal session on potential litigation. On the practical side, the Council set next year's spending limits, updated financial policy, adopted a 5-year water management and drought planning update, and approved capital projects including work on the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot, and South Bay salt pond restoration.
keyTopics: Closed-door legal session on two potential lawsuits against the city
Proclamations for Immigrant Heritage Month, Kiwanis Club's 100th anniversary, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's judgeship
Setting the city's legal spending limit and updating budget policy for 2026-27
Adopting the updated 5-year water supply and drought contingency plan
Approving construction projects: Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and South Bay salt pond restoration

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: Sunnyvale's City Council meets on July 28, 2026, starting with a closed-door session followed by a study session focused on updating the city's policy for artificial turf fields. The council will also handle routine business, including approving city bill payments, extending a contract for landfill services, and authorizing unpaid utility bills to be collected via property tax bills.
keyTopics: Study session on updating the Artificial Turf Policy
Renewing the landfill services contract with SCS Field Services, Inc.
Placing unpaid utility charges onto residents' 2026/27 county property tax bills
Routine approval of city claims and bill payments
Review of upcoming council meeting schedule and board/commission minutes

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — July 21, 2026
cupertino.summary: The City Council met in a closed, private session to discuss three ongoing lawsuits against the City of Cupertino with their attorneys. No public discussion or votes on the merits of these cases happen in open session; the council simply consulted with legal counsel on litigation strategy.
keyTopics: Lawsuit: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino
Lawsuit: Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino
Lawsuit: Garden Gate Coalition for Mary Avenue Safety v. City of Cupertino
Closed-door legal strategy session with city attorneys

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — June 9, 2026
santa-clara.summary: Santa Clara's City Council held a public hearing to approve the city's budget plans for the next two years, including money for building and repair projects, updates to this year's operating budget, and separate budgets for the Housing Authority and the Sports and Open Space Authority. This meeting essentially locks in how the city will spend taxpayer money on infrastructure, housing programs, and public spaces through mid-2028.
keyTopics: Adoption of the FY 2026/27 and FY 2027/28 two-year Capital Improvement Program budget (funding for roads, facilities, and other infrastructure projects)
Approval of changes to the current FY 2026/27 operating budget
Adoption of the FY 2026/2027 Housing Authority budget
Adoption of the FY 2026/2027 Sports and Open Space Authority budget

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — April 7, 2026
milpitas.summary: Milpitas City Council met to consider changes to how federal housing and community development funds are allocated, including a proposed amendment to the city's 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2025-2026 funding plan. Council members also reviewed a list of new project ideas submitted by individual councilmembers and discussed a proposed change to the rules for filling a vacant council seat, including shortening the process timeline.
keyTopics: Proposed amendment to the 2025-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2025-2026 funding allocations (likely tied to federal housing/community development grants)
New project and policy ideas proposed by individual councilmembers for the city's workplan
Proposed ordinance change to how council vacancies are filled, including reducing the timeline
Upcoming council meeting calendar and schedule
Approval of previous meeting minutes and preview of items for the next council meeting

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — July 8, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The City Council opened with routine business (director's report, schedule, and committee assignments), then held a public hearing on a rezoning request for 470 Olive Avenue. The proposal would change the property from single-family residential zoning to medium-density mixed-use zoning, aligning it with the neighboring parcel at 2951 El Camino Real, as part of the North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan.
keyTopics: Rezoning of 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential (NV-R1) to medium-density mixed-use (NV-MXM)
Amendment to the North Ventura Coordinated Area Plan land use designation
Aligning zoning with the adjacent 2951 El Camino Real parcel
Director's report and upcoming meeting schedule
Council committee assignments
